chains.title: GATA2 binding at the ref allele contributes to LMO1 regulation
chains.element: The variant lies in a candidate distal enhancer-like element.

links.claim: GATA2 is the leading candidate: it is strongly expressed and ChIP-bound over the variant in SK-N-SH, and its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref C than alt A. GATA3 is also occupied and has a significant ref-favoring result in its own model, but is less expressed; binding evidence alone does not establish which factor mediates the regulatory effect.
The variant is inside cCRE EH38E1518342, annotated as distal enhancer-like; the reported chromatin scores are maxima across biosamples, not evidence of enhancer activity in SK-N-SH.

LMO1 is the favored target, based on the intronic location, gene-link scores favoring LMO1 over RIC3, and literature connecting the intronic GATA motif to LMO1 expression; regulation of LMO1 by this particular cCRE is not established.

GATA2 occupancy and high expression are documented in SK-N-SH, while the locus has been implicated in the adrenergic neuroblastoma cell state; the full proposed mechanism has not been demonstrated in that state.

This model predicts that stronger GATA2 binding on ref C supports LMO1 regulation associated with neuroblastoma susceptibility, with alt A corresponding to the protective allele direction reported for the complementary T allele; GATA2-specific mediation and the binding-to-expression direction remain unproven.

predictions: GATA2-specific depletion should reduce the variant-dependent LMO1 regulatory output more than GATA3-specific depletion does.
In a relevant neuroblastoma context, ref C should show stronger GATA2 binding than alt A, and precise C-to-A editing should alter LMO1 regulation in the predicted direction.
falsified_if: GATA2-specific depletion leaves the allele-dependent LMO1 output unchanged while GATA3-specific depletion removes it.
Precise editing and allele-aware assays show no reproducible GATA2-dependent difference in occupancy or LMO1 regulation.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs2168101
predictions: The variant may be a marker of another causal change, or the predicted in-vitro binding differences may not cause a regulatory effect in cells.
Precise editing of rs2168101 alone should not reproducibly change LMO1 regulation or a neuroblastoma-relevant phenotype.

grades_v0.reason: GATA2 occupancy over the variant is reported in SK-N-SH, and its own QBiC-SELEX model shows a strong, significant change favoring ref C. Its higher expression than GATA3 and use of its own model support prioritizing it, though neither establishes that it causes the regulatory effect.
E03 places the variant inside the named dELS cCRE and lists LMO1 among nearby genes. This supports a candidate enhancer-like element, not experimentally demonstrated enhancer activity toward LMO1.

The variant is intronic to LMO1, credible-set L2G scores favor LMO1 over RIC3, and the cited literature connects the intronic GATA motif to LMO1 expression. These support LMO1 as the favored target, though not as a proven target of this cCRE.

GATA2 occupancy and expression are directly documented in SK-N-SH. The cited literature also links the locus to an adrenergic neuroblastoma state, although it does not establish the full mechanism specifically in SK-N-SH.

The cited zebrafish result supports a risk-versus-protective allele direction consistent with ref G/C versus alt T/A. But the claim that stronger GATA2 binding raises LMO1 expression and thereby causes susceptibility remains an inference; the cited evidence does not establish GATA2-specific mediation or the allele-to-expression direction.

GATA3 occupancy over the variant and expression in SK-N-SH are documented, and the mapped QBiC-SELEX model predicts greater binding to ref C. However, that model is a GATA2 model and does not establish GATA3-specific recognition; the evidence therefore supports shared GATA-family motif sensitivity more than a GATA3-specific binding change.

GATA3 occupancy and expression are directly documented in SK-N-SH. The cited literature links the locus to an adrenergic neuroblastoma state, but does not demonstrate GATA3-specific action in that state.

The allele direction is consistent with the cited zebrafish risk-versus-protective result, but the evidence does not establish that GATA3 mediates the effect or that GATA3 binding changes LMO1 expression.

GATA3 depletion preferentially removes the allele-dependent LMO1 output; GATA2 depletion has a smaller effect.

matrix.test: Allele-aware GATA2 and GATA3 occupancy assay at rs2168101 in heterozygous neuroblastoma cells

outcomes.outcome: Ref C is preferentially occupied by GATA2; this would support, but not prove, GATA2 mediation.
Ref C is preferentially occupied by GATA3; this would support, but not prove, GATA3 mediation.
No reproducible allele-specific occupancy is detected for either factor.

matrix.test: Precise C-to-A editing followed by measurement of LMO1 expression and neuroblastoma-relevant cell-state output

outcomes.outcome: Editing changes LMO1 output in the predicted direction, with the change dependent on GATA2.
Editing changes LMO1 output in the predicted direction, with the change dependent on GATA3.
Editing alone produces no reproducible change in LMO1 output or relevant cell-state output.

next_experiment: The cheapest direct discriminator is a parallel, factor-specific GATA2 versus GATA3 depletion experiment in SK-N-SH, measuring allele-dependent LMO1 RNA or enhancer output. A preferential loss after GATA2 depletion favors H1; after GATA3 depletion favors H2. Include non-targeting controls and verify depletion of each factor.

Our data suggest that LMO1 overexpression in MYCN-amplified NB cells increases the pro-metastatic properties of macrophages in the tumor-cell microenvironment, which is important for driving NB metastasis.
We found LMO1 rs2168101 G > T and rs11603024 C > T as well as LMO2 rs7933499 G > A were significantly associated with Wilms tumor risk.

Fourteen loci, including ten protective polymorphisms from CASC15, BARD1, LMO1, HSD17B12, and HACE1, and four risk variants from BARD1, RSRC1, CPZ and MMP20 were significantly associated with neuroblastoma risk.
Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.

Here, we showed that WT zebrafish with the GATA genotype developed adrenergic neuroblastoma, while knock-in of the protective TATA allele at this locus reduced the penetrance of MYCN-driven tumors, which were restricted to the mesenchymal cell state.
They now demonstrate experimentally, using genome-edited zebrafish, that a polymorphism in the human rs2168101 locus of the LMO1 gene determines which CRC is active in a tumor.

Shown: 10 of 12 occupied (5 with a strong site), 5 of 115 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 30 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 529 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 2 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.
Thus, conversion of the regulatory GATA to a TATA allele in the first intron of LMO1 reduced the neuroblastoma-initiation rate by preventing formation of the adrenergic cell state.
They now demonstrate experimentally, using genome-edited zebrafish, that a polymorphism in the human rs2168101 locus of the LMO1 gene determines which CRC is active in a tumor.
